sleeping.goal: Cure the sleeping smith, or break his keeping light
sleeping.journal: Under the floor of an old home I found a smith asleep in a cell, a red light burning on the wall over him. He has the blight in him, and the light holds it. The husks walking the rooms upstairs wear what is left of a household's clothes.

noted.keeping_rested: The husks upstairs were a household once, a woman and her children by the look of them. I put them down while he slept, and the house is quiet now.

cured_asleep.goal: Wait for the smith to wake
cured_asleep.journal: I gave {giver} the cure while he slept. He never stirred.

noted.keeping_rested: The husks upstairs were a household once, a woman and her children by the look of them. I put them down while he slept, and the house is quiet now.

his_day.goal: Cure the smith before the day is out

journal.?mark:keeping_turned: The light went out and nobody brought {giver} the cure in time.
journal.?: The light went out and {giver} woke coughing. I got the cure into him before his day was out.

?mark:keeping_rested: You. You came down for me. I heard the light go and thought, well, that's the end of it. And here you are, and the cold's going out of my hands.
I went up. I had to. I thought I'd find them at the door still, the way I left them. The rooms were quiet. They are at rest, all of them. That was you.

I couldn't do it. I had the hammer in my hand and I couldn't, so I went under the floor and lit the light instead. You did what I owed them. I'm a smith, it's all I've got worth giving. Tell me what you want and I'll make it to your measure.
?: You. You came down for me. I heard the light go and thought, well, that's the end of it. And here you are, and the cold's going out of my hands.
Don't go up with me. Those were mine, up there. My wife. The boys. If any of them are still walking, leave them to me, now I can lift a hammer again. I should have done it before I lay down.
I'm a smith. It's all I've got that's worth giving. Tell me what you want for it and I'll make it to your measure.

iron.say: Iron, then. Good honest iron, and I've a little put by. Which piece?

replies.journal: {giver} is making me a helmet in iron.
{giver} is making me a chestplate in iron.
{giver} is making me leggings in iron.
{giver} is making me boots in iron.

diamond.say: Show me, then. Which piece? A helmet takes five, a chestplate eight, leggings seven and boots four.

replies.journal: I gave {giver} 5 diamonds. He is making me a helmet from them.
I gave {giver} 8 diamonds. He is making me a chestplate from them.
I gave {giver} 7 diamonds. He is making me leggings from them.
I gave {giver} 4 diamonds. He is making me boots from them.

forging.journal: {giver} is back at his forge. He said to come back in a day or two.

collect.goal: Collect what the smith made you
say: There. Try it on. If it pinches, it's your fault for growing.
I keep the old rite over everything I make, the same words that kept me. It won't rust on you.
The forge is lit again. Come back when you need more. You'll pay like anyone else, but you'll get a master's work.

?mark:keeping_rested: I've been sick, they tell me. Asleep under the floor of my own house, and I don't remember a day of it.
Cured me? In my sleep? Anyone could walk in here and say that. And somebody has been upstairs. The rooms are quiet. They are at rest, all of them.
If that was you, then I thank you for them. It's more than I managed. But I'll not be told tales about the other. Go on, now. Leave me with them.
?: I've been sick, they tell me. Asleep under the floor of my own house, and I don't remember a day of it.
Cured me? In my sleep? Anyone could walk in here and say that. I'll thank you not to tell me tales. Out of my house.

turned.text: Nobody got the cure into {giver} in time. He rose as one of the dead, like his household upstairs. The keeping only ever bought him time.

unbelieved.text: {giver} woke well and never believed I was the one who cured him. I got nothing for it but the walk.

waived.text: {giver} wanted to make me something for the cure. I told him to get his strength back first. His forge is lit again, and he sells a master's work at the old home.

lines: I've put them in the ground behind the house, all of them, under the one stone. I cut their names myself. It took me four days, which is slow for a smith.
I wanted you to know where they are, since you were the last one kind to them. If you pass this way, the forge is lit and there's a seat by it.

diamond_helmet.text: {giver} forged me a helmet in diamond for the cure, made to my measure.
